default.content:
Spaced repetition

Reviewing material at expanding intervals (1d, 3d, 7d, 30d) exploits the spacing effect: each successful recall just before forgetting strengthens retention far more than re-reading. Anki and similar systems schedule the next review from recall quality.

Tailscale ACLs

ACLs gate which tailnet nodes can reach which ports. Tags replace a node's user identity with a role identity so servers keep access when people leave; rules then say 'group:admins can reach tag:server on port 22'.

Ada Nest — hub

Hub lesson for the ada-nest-* topic family (the member-node heartbeat/monitoring design). Sub-topics get their own ada-nest-<topic> lessons; this page keeps the family inventory.

# Ada voice session benchT1
## User [09:01:10]
what's the difference between TCP BBR and CUBIC congestion control?
## Ada [09:01:12]
CUBIC is loss-based — it grows the congestion window until packet loss, then backs off, which fills buffers and adds latency. BBR is model-based: it measures bottleneck bandwidth and round-trip time and paces sends to sit at that operating point instead of filling buffers. In practice BBR keeps latency lower on buffer-bloated links; CUBIC can win on short high-bandwidth paths.

# Ada voice session benchT3
## User [09:12:03]
how do tailscale ACLs work again — what's the difference between a tag and a regular ACL rule?
## Ada [09:12:06]
An ACL rule says which sources can reach which destinations and ports. A tag is an identity you put on a device instead of a user — tagged devices stop being owned by a person, so servers keep access when users leave. You write rules like 'group:admins can reach tag:server on port 22' — the tag becomes the node identity.

# Ada voice session benchT4
## User [09:20:11]
what is the CAP theorem in distributed systems?
## Ada [09:20:13]
CAP says a distributed data store under a network partition must choose between consistency and availability — you can't guarantee both while partitioned. In practice you pick CP (refuse writes, stay consistent) or AP (keep serving, reconcile later); when there is no partition you get both, so the real decision is what to do during failures.

# Ada voice session benchT6
## User [09:40:22]
how does the ada nest heartbeat escalation actually work — when does a member node page me?
## Ada [09:40:25]
Each member sends a heartbeat every interval and the hub watches freshness. If a member misses N beats its state goes stale, then degraded; only after the degraded window passes without recovery does it escalate to a page — so a single missed beat or a brief wifi flap never reaches your phone.
